subject: general
question: Which of the following is true when you delete a file and it is placed in the Recycle Bin on Windows?

options.text: The file is permanently removed from the system and cannot be restored.
The file is moved to the system's storage space but remains inaccessible until permanently deleted.
The file remains locked and cannot be accessed or deleted further.
The file can be restored by right-clicking it and selecting the 'Restore' option.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The file can be restored by right-clicking it and selecting the 'Restore' option.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a file is deleted in Windows, it is typically moved to the Recycle Bin instead of being permanently erased from the system.
 
• The Recycle Bin acts as a temporary storage area for deleted files, allowing users to restore them if needed.
 
• Files in the Recycle Bin can be restored by right-clicking on the file and selecting the 'Restore' option, which returns the file to its original location.
 
• Until permanently deleted, files in the Recycle Bin continue to occupy storage space on the system.
 
• The Recycle Bin serves as a safeguard against accidental file deletions, offering users the ability to recover files easily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recycle Bin:** A feature in Windows operating systems designed to temporarily store deleted files and folders until they are permanently removed.
 
• **Permanently Deleting Files:** Files can be permanently removed from the system by emptying the Recycle Bin or using the "Shift + Delete" command.
 
• **Storage Space:** The Recycle Bin occupies a portion of the hard disk space, which can be configured by the user based on their storage requirements.
 
• **Restoration Process:** Restoring files from the Recycle Bin reverts them to their original location on the system, ensuring minimal data loss.
 
• **File Locking:** Files in the Recycle Bin are not locked and can be permanently deleted or restored at any time by the user.
